title: Choose the visual world for SplitBill
question: The roll assigned the Pinto (enamel tiffin carrier) direction. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Pinto
options.lineage: Thai enamel pinto tiffin carriers, one meal shared in stacked tiers
options.thesis: Every bill is one carrier and every roommate's share is a tier stacked to the exact total.
options.viewport: Deep enamel-green household rail on the left; your balance hero and the bill stack on top; expenses as a dense table below; the new-bill form opens as a side panel with a live tier stack.
options.risk: If the tiers read as decoration rather than data, it becomes a cute food metaphor; stacks must stay proportional and labelled.

raised.raise: Enamel colours are reserved for one job only: identifying a roommate, everywhere.
The carrier has a fixed height: an exact split can't overflow, and the unfilled tier shows as an open dashed gap.
Every amount sits in strict tabular columns, right-aligned to the satang.

options.label: Skytrain Line
options.thesis: A household is a line on the map, and each roommate is a station showing where they stand.
options.viewport: Top bar with line-coloured household tabs; a horizontal line diagram of members with balances under each station; expenses table below.
options.risk: The most familiar reading of Bangkok; bilingual signage is where most runs would land.

options.label: Terminal Yellow
options.thesis: Each balance as the next decision on a yellow band.
options.viewport: Yellow band with your balance at monumental scale.
options.case: Loses both axes: roommates settling monthly aren't in a rush to a gate.

options.label: Mixtape J-card
options.thesis: Expenses as a tracklist that must fit the tape.
options.viewport: Side A / side B halves of the month.
options.case: Loses both axes: nostalgia without household meaning.
options.kept: A fixed capacity that visibly can't overflow.

options.label: Bitmap Specimen
options.thesis: The balance set as pixel display type.
options.viewport: Giant pixel balance over dense columns.
options.case: Loses both axes: no household identification; Thai has no bitmap tradition here.
options.kept: One form repeated consistently at several sizes.

options.label: Event Catalog
options.thesis: Expenses as a packed numbered grid.
options.case: Loses both axes: a grid hides the running ledger.
options.kept: Density courage in the expense list.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Colour codes stand in for names.
options.viewport: Black field with a coded member strip.
options.case: Loses both axes: coding names makes a shared ledger harder to read.
options.kept: Colour as a consistent identity code.

options.label: Datamatics
options.thesis: The ledger as a strobing data field.
options.viewport: Black field of bars and numbers.
options.case: Loses both axes: cold and anxious for a household tool.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A Splitwise-style finance app executed cleanly.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar of groups, summary cards on top, expense list below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other expense splitter by design.
